'''Heinrich Hora''' (born 1 July 1931) is a German-Australian [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]. He made contributions to [[solid state physics]], optical properties of plasma with relativistic and quantum effects and nonlinear dynamics with applications of [[lasers]] for producing [[nuclear fusion]] energy. He lives in Sydney where he is an emeritus professor at the [[University of New South Wales]] and a former vice-president of the [[Royal Society of New South Wales]].

== Early life ==
Heinrich Hora was born on 1 July 1931 in [[Děčín|Podmokly]], [[Czechoslovakia]]. He received the degree Diplom-Physiker from the Martin-Luther-University, Halle-Wittenberg, Germany, in 1956, and the Dr. Rer Nat. from the Friedrich-Schiller-University, Jena, Germany. In 1981 the University of New South Wales, Australia, awarded him the D.Sc. degree. <ref> 1. Eliezer, S. et al. On the Surface Tension of Plasmas. IEEE Trans. Plasma Sci. 17, 284–289 (1989). </ref>

== Academic career and achievements ==
As foundation professor of theoretical physics at the [[University of New South Wales]] from 1975 and emeritus from 1992 he established the Department of Theoretical Physics, where a number of students received the [[University Medal|university medal]], with a record level of publications and where he supervised most of his 25 PhD students. Guest and adjunct professorships include ones at the [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]], the universities of Rochester, Bern, Iowa, Giessen, Tokyo, Regensburg, Osaka, Western Sydney and the Weizmann Institute. For seven years he was active in industrial research at Zeiss, IBM, Westinghouse and Siemens. He also was involved with research for 12 years at the Max-Planck-Institute for Plasma Physics in [[Garching]] near [[Munich]], Germany and for one year as attache remun. at [[CERN]] (Conseil Européen pour la Recherche Nucléaire, or European Council for Nuclear Research) in [[Geneva]], Switzerland.

He consulted [[Rainer Erler]] to the laser movie "Der Verräter" in the TV series "[[Das Blaue Palais]]". His taped lecture course at CERN (1991) about laser acceleration of particles contributed to [[Gerard Mourou]]'s PeV particle acceleration.

His discoveries include the volume mechanism for photo-electric emission, sub-threshold defect generation by electron beams for producing semiconductor junctions with application in [[solar cells]]. Prof. Hora's first publication about growth of diamond crystals by physical vapour deposition became an IBM patent in 1964. His first general formula for [[Nuclear power|nuclear energy]] gain at laser compression and thermal ignition of fusion led to his subsequent discovery of volume ignition (later confirmed by [[John Archibald Wheeler]] as "Wheeler modes"). Against established knowledge, he discovered electron acceleration in vacuum by lasers based on nonlinearity.<ref>H. Hora, Nature 333 (1988) 337</ref> His derivation of the nonlinear (ponderomotive) forces of laser-plasma interaction including dielectric effects in the Maxwellian stress tensor led to the prediction of ultrahigh acceleration of plasma blocks<ref>H. Hora Physics of Laser Driven Plasmas Wiley New York (1981) p. 179</ref> being confirmed experimentally by Sauerbrey<ref>R. Sauerbrey, Physics of Plasmas 3 (1996) 4712</ref> with application to a new laser fusion energy scheme as block ignition of uncompressed fuel<ref>H. Hora, J. Badziak et al.Physics of Plasmas 14 (2007) 072701</ref> resulting in a possible nuclear energy production with less radioactivity than burning coal.<ref>H. Hora, G.H.. Miley et al. Energy and Environmental Science 3 (2010) 479</ref><ref>H. Hora Climatic Problems and Solutions (in German), S. Roderer, Regensburg 2010</ref> He discovered the general mechanism of ponderomotive and relativistic self-focusing. His theory for crossing electron and laser beams within media (Schwarz-Hora effect)<ref>H. Hora Laser and Particle Beams, R.A. Mayers ed. Encyclopedia of Physical Sciences and Technology, Academic Press, San Diego, Vol. 7, 99–128 (1987); Vol. 8, 433–465 (1992)</ref><ref>H. Hora, P.H. Handel Kapitza-Dirac effect with lasers and non-resonant interaction for quantum modulation of electron beams (Schwarz-Hora effect) Applied Physics Letters 102 (2013) 141119</ref> led to the discovery of the [[correspondence principle]] of electromagnetic interaction and following [[Nathan Rosen]] to nonlocality and quantum entangling. Based on the importance of including usually neglected very tiny quantities as the longitudinal field components of laser beams led to the formulation of the nonlinearity principle showing how nonlinear physics is changing from wrong linear physics into correct understanding.<ref>R. Feynman in H. Hora Climatic Problems and Solutions (in German), S. Roderer, Regensburg 2010 p. 147</ref><ref>H. Hora, Laser Plasma Physics – Forces and the Nonlinearity Principle. Spie Press 2000, Bellingham, WA,</ref>

Hora initiated advanced schemes of laser driven fusion energy and became Director of the  foundation of SAFE (Society to Advance Fusion Energy) with the president Luella LaMeer Slaner from the traditional billionaires North of Manhattan and [[George H. Miley]] as executive director, to push through a law for spending $20 billion for nuclear fusion research finally signed by President [[Jimmy Carter]] in 1980.<ref>Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents, Vol. 16, No. 14, Oct. 7 1980, Public Law 96-386</ref> This led finally to the scheme of laser pulses of 30 kilojoule energy to produce gigajoule energy from the clean reaction of uncompressed proton-boron fuel<ref>Hora, H., Eliezer, S., Kirchhoff, G. J., Nissim, N., Wang, J. X., Lalousis, P., ... & Kirchhoff, J. (2017). Road map to clean energy using laser beam ignition of boron-hydrogen fusion. Laser and Particle Beams, 35(4), 730-740.</ref> resulting in less radioactivity than burning coal.

By 2017 he and associated startup [[HB11]] had committed to [[hydrogen-boron fusion]]
and in February 2020 announced patents on the technique using a [[petawatt]] [[laser]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/science/australian-fusion-startup-unlimited-energy-591445|title = Australian fusion startup promises unlimited, safe energy|date = 22 February 2020}}</ref>

== Family and personal life ==

Heinrich Hora and his late wife Rosemarie Hora † 2007, née Weiler, have six children, sixteen grandchildren and six great-grandchildren. [[File:Heinrich Hora's marriage in 1956.jpg|thumb|Heinrich Hora's marriage in 1956]]

== Degrees and awards ==

D. Sc. ([[University of New South Wales|UNSW]]), Dr. rer. nat. ([[University of Jena|Jena]]), Dipl. Physiker ([[University of Halle-Wittenberg|Halle-Wittenberg]]), FAIP, FInstP (London), FRSN

Ritter-von-Gerstner Medal (1985)
Edward-Teller Medal (1991)
[[Dirac Medal and Lecture|Dirac Medal]] of the [[University of New South Wales]] (2001)
Ernst-Mach Medal (2002)

== Books ==

===Editor===
* Founder and editor-in-chief of "Laser and Particle Beams", [[Cambridge University Press]] (1982–1991)
* Co-editor of P.A.M. Dirac "Direction of Physics", Wiley, New York 1978 (also Russian and Japanese)
* Co-editor of "Edward Teller Lectures", [[Imperial College London]] 2005
* Founder and co-editor of Conference Series "Laser Interaction and Related Plasma Phenomena", Plenum Press New York, 12 volumes 1971–1992
